# Hidden Roof

> Hidden Roof is a free multiplayer graffiti game in your browser — paint ink-drawn rooftops alone or with your friends.

A first-person game: you climb onto the rooftops of a city drawn in ink, and the only color in it is the paint you bring.

There are no enemies and no goals: find your tools, paint whatever you like, scrub it off, paint again. Play alone, or bring friends into a multiplayer session and paint the same roof together.

- Play: https://roof.hidden.haus/
- Creator: GeoGeorgeous, one developer, under the Hidden Haus name, using three.js.
- Free, in the browser: no ads, no purchases, no account, no install.
- First released on 9 October 2026. The source code is on GitHub under the Hidden Roof Source-Available License.
- Inspired by [Bombing!!: A Graffiti Sandbox and Bombing!! 2](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1527520/), [Marc Eckō's Getting Up: Contents Under Pressure](https://store.steampowered.com/app/260190/) and Daisuke Tajima's [Beyond the Lines](https://www.seigensha.com/books/978-4-86152-902-3/).

## Playing

- Needs a desktop or laptop browser with WebGL2, a keyboard, a mouse and a window at least 820×560. Phones, tablets and controllers are not supported.
- One level: a large rooftop, the same in solo and multiplayer, with new walls, windows, signs and props in updates.
- Every surface is paintable: brick, glass, metal, doors, staircases, even the floor. If you can reach it, you can paint it.
- You start with a spray can and black paint. Twelve more colors, five more caps and four more tools are hidden around the roof. Paint never runs out.
- Every key can be rebound in Settings → Controls. Settings → Graphics has a performance test that says what to change on a slow computer.

## Solo and multiplayer

- Solo: the whole roof to yourself, and the game pauses when you do.
- Public sessions: open to everyone, up to 40 players. Their paint stays on the server, so the walls fill up over days.
- Private sessions: up to 4 players, joined by a code. Their paint is lost once the last player leaves.
- Everyone in a session shares the same walls, and every stroke appears in real time. Other players can paint over or scrape off your work, and the admin may ban repeat offenders.
- You can download your roof's paint as a file and upload it later for a new session.

## Painting

- A stroke lays a continuous line of paint under the aim, with no gaps at any hand speed, not a cloud of dots. Passes add up.
- Distance: up close the line is narrow and crisp; stepping back makes it wider and softer.
- Hand speed: slow strokes are dense and sharp; fast ones are lighter, wider and softer.
- Angle: sprayed at an angle, paint stretches along the aim and fades towards the far end.
- Opacity: hold Run (Shift by default) and scroll, from 5% to 100%, on the can only. The can never loses pressure; shaking it is only an animation.
- Drips: wet paint that builds up in one place darkens, then runs slowly down the surface. Paint dries in seconds. Heavier coverage runs longer; the marker and the roller can trigger runs too.
- Crosshair: as wide as the line would land, with the set opacity on an arc; it fades where paint won't reach.
- Plume: every cap has its own soft plume at the nozzle, from a thin jet to a wide cloud. It follows the opacity, and other players see it too.
- Streamline (Settings → General) smooths lines: the brush trails the aim a little. Painting has its own mouse sensitivity and field of view.

## Caps

Q and E switch between them by default. Every player starts with BANANA; the others are found on the roof.

- NEEDLE: ultra-fine lines for sharp details and highlights.
- SKINNY: clean tags and crisp outlines.
- BANANA: a versatile all-rounder for everyday painting.
- BLUE DOT: soft edges for smooth blends and fades.
- NY FAT: wide lines for throw-ups and quick fills.
- ASTRO FAT: massive coverage for big fills and backgrounds.

## Tools

All found on the roof. Q and E change the width of the first three by default.

- Marker: a square nib for crisp lines and letters, up to 10 cm wide.
- Roller: solid bands of paint on a short pole that reaches 5 m, from 20 to 80 cm wide. It rolls up and down, and its paint runs easily.
- Sponge: scrapes off any paint, from 4 to 60 cm wide. One pass fades it, scrubbing cleans it, and holding Crouch scrubs the floor.
- Stepladder: stands on the floor and reaches high walls. Each player has one, and in a session others can climb it.

## Sound

- Real recordings of the city at night from a rooftop, of rain and of thunder, along with footsteps, air conditioners and the can's hiss. In a room the city gets muffled and the rain changes to rain on a tin roof.
- The can's hiss gets louder with more opacity, closer to the wall and with the hand moving, and every cap has its own loudness and tone.
